title: Check if Every Row and Column Contains All Numbers
spaceBreakdown:
- vector<bool> seen: n+1 entries → O(n)
- recursion depth: none
- not counted: input matrix, returned bool
approach: For each row, mark which values 1..n appear using a boolean array, then verify all are present; repeat for each column. Since values are guaranteed in [1, n], a row/column is valid iff every value 1..n appears at least once (equivalently exactly once, since there are n cells). Reusing one boolean array of size n+1 across all checks keeps auxiliary space at O(n).
hints: A valid row of length n must contain exactly the integers 1 through n. What must be true about how many distinct values appear in such a row?
Use a boolean array of size n+1 as a set. For row [1,2,3] with n=3, mark seen[1], seen[2], seen[3] true, then confirm all of seen[1..3] are true; repeat per column.

```
for each row i:
    reset seen
    for each column j: seen[matrix[i][j]] = true
    if any seen[1..n] is false: return false
for each column j:
    reset seen
    for each row i: seen[matrix[i][j]] = true
    if any seen[1..n] is false: return false
return true
```

**Smallest input** - n = 1, single cell
`Input: [[1]]` → `Expected: true`
⚠️ Bug: looping k from 0 to n-1 instead of 1 to n → returns false (seen[0] is never set)

**Duplicate row that sums correctly** - row of all 2s sums to 6 = 1+2+3
`Input: [[2,2,2],[1,2,3],[1,2,3]]` → `Expected: false`
⚠️ Bug: checking only that each row sum equals n(n+1)/2 → returns true (2+2+2 = 6 = 1+2+3)

**Forgotten reset** - seen array carries over between rows
`Input: [[1,2,3],[1,1,1],[1,1,1]]` → `Expected: false`
⚠️ Bug: not clearing seen between rows → returns true (all entries still true from row 0)

**Column check skipped** - rows valid but a column is not
`Input: [[1,2,3],[2,3,1],[2,3,1]]` → `Expected: false`
⚠️ Bug: checking only rows and skipping columns → returns true (column 0 is [1,2,2], missing 3)

followUps.q: If n can be up to 10^5 and rows arrive one at a time from a stream, how do you keep memory low?
followUps.a: Process each row as it arrives using a single boolean array of size n+1, resetting between rows; columns cannot be checked in a single pass, so you'd need to maintain n column-sets (or bitsets) in parallel, giving O(n²/64) bits ≈ O(n²) memory for the column accumulators.

followUps.q: What if values can repeat and you must verify each value 1..n appears exactly once per row/column?
followUps.a: Replace the boolean array with an integer count array of size n+1; after scanning a row/column, confirm every count equals 1. Time stays O(n²), space stays O(n).

followUps.q: Can you solve it in O(1) extra space without modifying the input?
followUps.a: Not in general - without extra storage you cannot track which of n values appeared. If modifying the input is allowed, sort each row and each column in place (O(n² log n) time, O(log n) stack) and check they equal [1,2,…,n].
